pr.title: Install the plugins Projector depends on before a Claude CI review, so the review-pr skill loads
pr.head: abe0fc37396a65cd84405063e65a49a37903dffc

summary: Projector can review pull requests in GitHub Actions: its actions/review action installs an agent's CLI on the runner and has it run Projector's review-pr skill. For Claude, the action gives Claude Code Projector's source as a plugin with --plugin-dir, and the plugin supplies the skill.

Projector's plugin manifest, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, lists gh-stack as a dependency, and Claude Code loads no plugin whose dependency is missing. The runner had no gh-stack, so the plugin never loaded and the agent never had the skill. Most agents found the skill's files and followed them anyway. One didn't, published no verdict, and failed its job.

This change adds three commands to the action's install step. They register Projector's own source tree as a plugin marketplace, a catalogue of plugins that .claude-plugin/marketplace.json describes, install gh-stack from it at the commit the catalogue pins, and update it, so a runner that kept an older copy moves to the pin. A test runs the install step against fake npm and claude commands, and the CI review documentation describes the step.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Marketplace: a catalogue of Claude Code plugins. Projector's lists Projector itself and gh-stack, pinned to a tag and commit.
  • Dependency: a plugin another plugin's manifest names. Claude Code refuses to load the dependent plugin until the dependency is installed.
  • Persistent runner: a self-hosted runner that keeps its files, ~/.claude included, from one job to the next.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The reviews of 98f788d and 341ad1b requested changes with one finding: on a persistent runner, claude plugin install leaves an older gh-stack in place after a Projector upgrade changes the pin. docs/self-hosted-runners.md documents self-hosted Claude runners that keep ~/.claude between jobs, so the finding applies today.

At abe0fc3 the step runs claude plugin update gh-stack@projector after the install, and the step's comment and the CI review guide say so. The review of abe0fc3 found the finding fixed and signed the head off.

groups.title: Install the dependencies before the review
groups.kicker: The action's install step adds the marketplace, then installs and updates gh-stack
intro: Right after the Claude Code CLI is installed, the action registers $PROJECTOR_ROOT, the Projector source tree the action runs from, as a marketplace. It then installs gh-stack@projector, meaning the gh-stack plugin from the marketplace named projector, and updates it. On a fresh runner the update finds nothing to do. On a runner that kept ~/.claude from an earlier job, install leaves the old copy as it is, and update brings it to the version this tree pins. With the dependency installed, the plugin that --plugin-dir passes loads, and with it the review-pr skill.
The Codex path needs nothing like this: the action links Projector's skills straight into the Codex home, and Codex checks no dependencies.

files.note: Three new commands in the claude branch of the Install the agent step.

checks.text: In an empty Claude Code 2.1.327 configuration, the three commands run twice against this tree all exit 0. The second run reports the marketplace on disk and the plugin installed, and both update runs report 0.2.1, the pinned version, as the latest. This review itself ran with the plugin loaded.

groups.title: Test and documentation
groups.kicker: A test of the install step's commands, and a sentence in the CI review guide
intro: The new test runs the action's install step with fake npm and claude commands that log how they're called. It checks that the step adds the marketplace before installing, that it installs each dependency the manifest names from a marketplace that carries that dependency, and that it runs update after install for each one. The existing helper's fake npm now leaves a fake agent CLI behind, so the new claude plugin calls have something to run.

files.note: Describes the new step under what each review job does.
